query_tool_wire.name: query
query_tool_wire.description: The one tool for questions that rank, list, total or compare players or teams on a statistic, over a window of matches, with filters, or that compare two sets of matches (for example with and without a player). Fill a field only with what the user stated; every constraint carries a `quote` copied from the user's message (at most 12 words each; give several short quotes as a list when the words are apart). Leave out anything the user did not say: unstated fields take declared defaults (list, player, sum, whole season, desc, top 10). A word of the question that states a constraint must be inside some quote. If the question asks for something this form cannot state, put it in not_expressible with its kind (single_value only when the question asks for ONE number, not a list); if a phrase is vague, put it in ambiguous. match_set is the FIRST set of matches and compare_to the SECOND (only with shape comparison). At team grain a named club ALWAYS goes in filters as club eq (grain alone does not select a club). Ownership as it was AT THAT TIME ('then', 'at the time', 'en ese momento', 'entonces') is not owned_now: report it in not_expressible with kind ownership_then. Dates: send the day and month as MM-DD; add the year (YYYY-MM-DD) ONLY when the user wrote a year. Operator plus adds two statistics: metric plus metric_plus. Example with/without: 'Team T xG with and without Player A' = shape comparison, grain team, filters [club eq 'Team T'], match_set [player_played_60 'Player A'], compare_to [player_absent 'Player A']. Example periods: 'goals in GW1-5 against GW6-10' = shape comparison, match_set [gw_range [1,5]], compare_to [gw_range [6,10]]. For player_played_60 and player_absent the quote is just the player's name. Unsupported-kind ids: player_venue, opponent, month, calendar_phrase, result, started, several_players, player_attribute, exclusion, single_value, difference_list, more_than_two_sets, ownership_then, future, flank_or_shots, past_season, count_of_gws, streak, vague_recent.

metric.description: The statistic asked for: an id from the list; at team grain use the team_ ids. If no id means what the user asked for, do not pick the nearest one: report it in not_expressible or ambiguous. Phrases that name one id: 'goles mas asistencias esperados' = expected_goal_involvements; 'goles y asistencias esperados' = expected_goal_involvements; 'goles mas asistencias esperadas' = expected_goal_involvements; 'goles y asistencias esperadas' = expected_goal_involvements; 'expected goal involvements' = expected_goal_involvements; 'goles mas asistencias' = operator plus, metric goals_scored, metric_plus assists; 'goals plus assists' = operator plus, metric goals_scored, metric_plus assists.

override_block:
RANKING-BY-METRIC OVERRIDE (highest tool-routing priority):
  - Any request to rank, order, list, total or compare players OR teams BY a named metric/statistic,
    over a season, one gameweek, the last N gameweeks, a range, since a date, with filters (position,
    price, club, ownership) or WITH vs WITHOUT a player (two sets of matches)
    → call query FIRST and as the ONLY tool. Fill only what the user stated, each with its quote.
  - Never choose another tool from keyword overlap in the metric (for example, do
    not choose a gameweek tool because the requested metric mentions gameweek/jornada).
  - If the metric is unfamiliar or no listed id means it, do not pick the nearest id: report it in
    not_expressible or ambiguous. Do not synthesize a ranking from other data or fail silently.

get_historical_gameweek_top_scorer: Goals over the WHOLE SEASON are rank_players_by_metric(goals_scored). Goals in ONE gameweek, the last N or a range have NO tool: say so plainly and never answer with points instead.
Goals, or any other statistic, over a season, ONE gameweek, the last N gameweeks or a range are the query tool (metric goals_scored): never answer with points instead.

web_off_line: WEB_OFF: web access is OFF this turn. web_fetch and search_web are not available: ignore every line above that tells you to fetch, search or open a page, or to offer to. ONLY when the question itself needs the web, or recent news that no tool returned, say so in ONE short sentence in the user's language (es: "Enciende la web para consultarlo." / en: "Turn on Web to check it."), then answer only from what the tools returned. Never add that sentence to an answer the tools already covered, and never use it as a closing line. Never claim you checked a page.
